data.narrative:
Wardstone is a seed-stage company in Space & Aerospace that has raised $5M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Starcloud, SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space.

Standard triangulation methods were tested but do not yield reliable results given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis, which would imply a $212M valuation, was rejected because it exceeds 20x the company's total raised capital—indicating the base value proxy is unreliable. Peer-median analysis cannot proceed: while 14 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters (identical stage, adjacent stage, similar valuation tier) yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3) to establish a defensible median. Public-comp anchoring using the sector's 24.4x P/S median cannot be applied because Wardstone's revenue is not disclosed, which is typical for private companies at this stage.

The absence of applicable triangulation methods reflects the inherent challenge of seed-stage space-tech valuation: limited financial disclosure, sparse peer data at identical stage-and-tier, and early-stage revenue opacity. A credible range cannot be established without either (1) disclosed or estimated revenue, (2) a denser peer set at seed stage, or (3) founder guidance on internal metrics. Further diligence on comparable seed financings or management projections is required to support valuation.
